html:
Bob Marley was a Jamaican singer and songwriter who took reggae to the whole world.

He was born in the village of Nine Mile in rural Jamaica, son of a Black Jamaican mother and a white father he barely knew. He grew up in Trenchtown, a poor district of Kingston. There he formed the Wailers with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer in the early 1960s, playing ska and then reggae.

Signed to Island Records, the band reached rock audiences with Catch a Fire (1973). Hits such as "No Woman, No Cry", "Get Up, Stand Up", "Redemption Song" and "One Love" followed, and the album Exodus (1977) made him a global star.

His songs carried the faith of Rastafari, with its devotion to Haile Selassie, and called for freedom for the poor and for Africa.

  • In 1978 his One Love Peace Concert brought Jamaica's two rival party leaders on stage to shake hands.
  • In 1980 he sang at the independence celebrations of Zimbabwe.

He died of cancer in 1981, aged 36. He remains the best known musician from the Caribbean.
sum: Bob Marley was a Jamaican singer and songwriter who took reggae to the whole world.
